questions.prompt: A listener is registered through research.ctx. Which announcements run it?
options: Announcements made through research's context only
Only announcements made through the root context
None, until it is moved to the root
questions.explanation: The listener carries the research tag. A dispatch through research's context admits untagged listeners and research-tagged ones; other scopes skip it.

questions.prompt: After research.dispose(), why is its listener gone?
options: The root clears every list when any scope closes
emit checks whether the scope still exists
Registering the listener was an effect on the scope's context, and disposing that context ran its disposers
Tagged listeners expire after one call
questions.explanation: on() is an effect recorded on the scope's own context. Disposing that context runs the disposers, which remove the entry.

questions.prompt: Which statement about agent scopes is accurate?
options: Scopes decide visibility and cleanup but are not a security boundary
Scopes stop an agent from reading any shared service
Scopes run each agent in a separate process
Scoped listeners always run before global ones
questions.explanation: A scope controls which registrations an agent sees and removes them with it. Code inside a scope can still reach the shared shelf.
